papers.title: One-Stop Automated Diagnostic System for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in Ultrasound Images Using Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Objective: Ultrasound (US) examination has unique advantages in diagnosing carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) while identifying the median nerve (MN) and diagnosing CTS depends heavily on the expertise of examiners. Methods: We combined real-time MN delineation, accurate biometric measurements, and explainable CTS diagnosis into a unified framework, called OSA-CTSD, evaluated on 32,301 static images from US videos of 90 normal wrists and 40 CTS wrists. Results: HD95 score of 7.21px, ASSD score of 2.64px, Dice score of 85.78%, and IoU score of 76.00%. Comparable with experienced radiologists and outperformed inexperienced radiologists (+3.59% accuracy, +5.85% F1).
papers.source_excerpt: Unified one-stop deep learning system (OSA-CTSD) combining real-time median nerve segmentation, biometric measurements, and explainable CTS diagnosis from ultrasound video frames.

papers.title: Diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome using deep learning with comparative guidance
papers.abstract: Developed a deep learning model using comparative classification of ultrasound images from the thenar and hypothenar muscles (median vs. ulnar nerve innervation zones) with cosine similarity-based comparative guidance to autonomously identify echotexture differences, proving robust against anatomical variations and standard CSA cutoff limitations.
papers.source_excerpt: Cosine similarity-based comparative guidance between thenar (median-innervated) and hypothenar (ulnar-innervated) muscle ultrasound images overcomes inter-patient anatomical variability.

papers.title: Explainable ultrasound-based multimodal deep learning for outcome prediction after needle release in carpal tunnel syndrome: a multicenter study
papers.abstract: Multicenter study combining pre-therapy sonographic features (cross-sectional area, transverse/longitudinal B-mode, color Doppler), electrophysiological parameters, and clinical data in an explainable multimodal deep learning framework to predict individual patient prognoses following ultrasound-guided needle release.
papers.source_excerpt: Multimodal deep learning fusing B-mode/Doppler ultrasound, electrophysiology, and clinical variables across multiple centers for post-needle-release prognosis prediction.

papers.title: Automated Ultrasound-Based Severity Classification of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: A Deep Learning Model Validated Against Nerve Conduction Studies
papers.abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) models trained on B-mode transverse and longitudinal ultrasound scans to automatically classify CTS severity into four levels (normal, mild, moderate, severe), validated against standardized nerve conduction studies (NCS) as the reference standard.
papers.source_excerpt: Four-class CTS severity grading (normal, mild, moderate, severe) directly from transverse and longitudinal B-mode ultrasound images anchored to NCS ground truth.

papers.title: Using Deep Learning for Ultrasound Images to Diagnose Carpal Tunnel Syndrome with High Accuracy
papers.abstract: Evaluated transfer learning with pre-trained CNN architectures to diagnose CTS directly from short-axis median nerve ultrasound images without manual or automated calculation of cross-sectional area (CSA), achieving up to 96% accuracy with Grad-CAM highlighting the epineurium and surrounding tissues.
papers.source_excerpt: CSA-free end-to-end CNN classification of short-axis carpal tunnel ultrasound images achieving up to 96% diagnostic accuracy.
